podcast.title: Origin and Location
podcast.body: The band Age of Electric originated from Regina and Lanigan, Saskatchewan, establishing their regional roots in the Canadian music scene. The Dahle brothers, Ryan and Kurt, were key members. "the band was from Regina and Lannigan's Saskatchewan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Member Activities
podcast.body: Following Age of Electric's original run, members pursued various projects: the Dahle brothers formed Limblifter, Todd Kerns became the bass player and backup vocalist for Slash in The Conspirators, and three other members joined Matthew Good's backup band. These transitions highlight the interconnectedness of Canadian musicians. "Todd Kerns from Age of Electric has been working as the bass player in Back of Vocalist for Slash, yes, as in Guns and Roses Slash, in his band The Conspirators."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Reunion and Re-issue
podcast.body: Age of Electric had a reunion show in Calgary in 2015, indicating a return to live performances. In 2017, their acclaimed album *Make a Pest a Pet* was re-issued, suggesting a renewed interest in their catalog. "there was an Age of Electric show in Calgary in 2015 and a re-issue of their best album, Make a Pest a Pet in 2017."

xref.title: Dahle Brothers' Additional Project
xref.body: Static and Stereo was another band formed by the Dahle brothers, Ryan and Kurt, showcasing their prolific musical collaboration beyond Age of Electric and Limblifter. Its mention implies a level of recognition among listeners. "The doll brothers had another band that you might remember called Static and Stereo."

xref.title: Formation and Early Success
xref.body: Limblifter was formed as an offshoot band by brothers Ryan and Kurt Dahle, who were previously in Age of Electric. They achieved several hits that extended their presence in the music scene through the early 2000s. "They formed an offshoot band called Limlifter. And they had some hits that extended through the early 2000s."
